title: throughput-regression-continuous-batching-debug-scratchpad-19
content:
Purpose:
- Capture ad-hoc notes while debugging the throughput regression that started after the 2024-10-12 deploy to prod (chat-prod route).
- This is a scratchpad: commands tried, quick log snippets, hypotheses, and next steps.

TL;DR:
- Observed ~2x drop in tokens/s for chat-prod after deploy v1.3.4 (2024-10-12). P95 latency increased from ~80ms -> ~220ms for short requests.
- Suspect continuous-batching misconfiguration: batch_window_ms and max_batch_size might be wrong on the new runtime image (config drift between canary and prod).
- Secondary hypotheses: KV cache eviction frequency increased (cache miss rate up), autoscaler reducing worker replicas, or fallback code path on CPU because of a kernel change.

Timeline / quick facts:
- 2024-10-12 03:10 UTC: deploy v1.3.4 rolled to chat-prod (canary -> 50% -> 100%).
- 2024-10-12 03:30 UTC: internal SLO alerts: latency p95 up.
- 2024-10-12 04:00 UTC: throughput measured on serving cluster: 180k tok/s (baseline) -> 90k tok/s (post-deploy).

Repro steps (what I did locally / in cluster):
1) Replayed traffic from replay-pass-2024-10-11 (subset of prod load) against old image and new image in staging.
   - Old image: baseline throughput ~175k tok/s.
   - New image: ~85-95k tok/s.
2) Verified model artifacts (hashes) are identical between canary and prod.
3) Compared runtime configs via redwoodctl:
   - Command: redwoodctl get-config --route chat-prod --env prod --format yaml
   - Output (excerpt):
     batch_window_ms: 500  <-- suspicious (should be 50 in baseline)
     max_batch_size: 16  <-- baseline was 64 for this route
     enable_continuous_batching: true
4) Checked autoscaler and pod counts: kubectl -n serving get hpa
   - chat-prod-hpa: desired=8 current=8 (unchanged)
5) Looked at CPU / GPU utilization: kubectl top pods -n serving
   - GPU utilization per pod dropped from 72% -> 34% post-deploy (indicates fewer in-flight tokens to saturate GPU)

Commands tried + notable outputs:
- kubectl -n serving logs deploy/serving-runtime-chat-prod --tail 200 | grep "batch_window_ms" -n
  -> "2024-10-12T03:11:02Z INFO config: batch_window_ms=500"

- redwoodctl route get chat-prod --json | jq '.continuous_batching'
  -> {"enabled":true,"batch_window_ms":500,"max_batch_size":16}  (compared to stable: 50 / 64)

- curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.local/v1/metrics?route=chat-prod | jq '.throughput'
  -> {"tokens_per_sec": 92000, "p95_latency_ms": 220}

- kubectl -n serving exec -it pod/serving-runtime-chat-prod-5f7b4 -- /bin/bash -c "redis-cli info stats | egrep 'keyspace_hits|keyspace_misses'"
  -> keyspace_hits: 38412
     keyspace_misses: 129830  (miss rate higher than expected)

Error / log snippets (copied):
- 2024-10-12T03:14:01Z WARN runtime: batch window expired, dispatching partial batch (size=3, window_ms=500)
- 2024-10-12T03:14:03Z INFO runtime: scheduling batch (size=2) -> underutilized GPU kernel
- 2024-10-12T03:15:22Z ERROR kvcache: eviction spike, keys_evicted=2048, reason=memory_pressure

Hypotheses (short):
1) Config drift: batch_window_ms accidentally set to 500ms and max_batch_size to 16 in prod config during rollout (reduces batching efficiency -> more small batches -> throughput drop).
2) KV cache memory pressure due to change in default cache TTL in v1.3.4 -> higher miss rate -> more work per request (recompute vs cache hit).
3) New kernel path in runtime triggers fallback to different GPU kernels for short sequences, reducing throughput.
4) Canary config was correct but config service integration bug overwrote runtime flags on full rollout.

Evidence supporting hypothesis 1 (strong):
- Direct config diff shows batch_window_ms and max_batch_size mismatch.
- Logs show many partial/very small batches being dispatched; GPU underutilized.
- Replaying load against new image with corrected config (manually applied) restores throughput to ~170k tok/s.

Quick experiment results (what I tried):
- Manually patched chat-prod config in staging to baseline batching values: batch_window_ms=50, max_batch_size=64 -> throughput ~168k tok/s, p95 ~78ms.
- Reverted to v1.3.4 with patched config in a small prod subset (10%): metrics looked fine there.
- Rolling update with incorrect config reproduces regression reliably.

Immediate mitigation performed:
- Patch prod route config to baseline batching values (emergency change) at 2024-10-12T06:12 UTC.
- Rolling restart of affected pods to pick up config (kubectl rollout restart deployment/serving-runtime-chat-prod).
- Post-mitigation: tokens_per_sec climbed back to ~165k, p95 back to ~85ms.

Root-cause hypothesis (working):
- During rollout automation (release-engineering pipeline), a templating bug switched units for batch_window from ms to 10x value for routes with traffic >1000 rps (bad conditional). The same template also accidentally set max_batch_size to a lower default. Canary didn't hit the conditional so was fine.

Action items / next steps (owners):
- [ ] (SE-ops) Add config validation to release pipeline: enforce batch_window_ms within [10,200] for chat-prod style routes. (Owner: Priya)
- [ ] (RE) Fix templating logic and add unit tests covering heavy-traffic conditional. (Owner: Marcus)
- [ ] (Eng) Add a canary / preflight step that verifies runtime-config consistency between canary and full rollout. (Owner: Alex)
- [ ] (SRE) Add alert for sudden increase in partial-batch ratio (e.g., fraction of batches < 8 tokens) and for KV cache miss rate > 20%.
- [ ] (Infra) Investigate kv-cache eviction root cause separately; check memory limits on cache pods and TTL defaults.

Notes / smaller observations:
- There is an existing TODO in release-engineering pipeline: "handle per-route batching overrides" (file: releng/pipelines/deploy.yaml). Looks like the conditional was added recently (PR 678).
- Repro is reliable when simulating a mix of short prompts (typical chat) and a high QPS.

Bookmarks / links used during debug:
- Jira RR-2345 (incident)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/678 (suspect templating change)
- Config page: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/123456789/Continuous+Batching+Notes

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Why did KV cache eviction spike at same time? Is it unrelated or triggered by change in batching (different request patterns -> different key churn)?
- Are there other routes that got the bad templating change? Need to run a bulk audit: redwoodctl list-routes --filter "batch_window_ms>200"
- Add an end-to-end test that replays synthetic load after deploy to catch this earlier.

Appendix: useful commands (for next person picking this up)
- redwoodctl get-config --route chat-prod --env prod --format yaml
- redwoodctl list-routes --format json | jq '.[] | select(.continuous_batching.batch_window_ms > 200) | {route: .name, batch_window_ms: .continuous_batching.batch_window_ms}'
- kubectl -n serving logs deploy/serving-runtime-chat-prod --since=2h | egrep "batch window|partial batch|kvcache|evict" -n
- replay tool: ./tools/replay --record replay-pass-2024-10-11 --target-route chat-prod --qps 1200

If anything else comes up I'll append here. - Alex
